I pulled these from the Algolia Hacker News API (`front_page` tag), so nothing was scraped. They are the top 5 front-page stories as of this query:

| # | Title | Points | URL |
|---|-------|--------|-----|
| 1 | Tesla Roadster | 1171 | https://www.tesla.com/roadster |
| 2 | Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins | 660 | https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins |
| 3 | 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks | 393 | https://www.mercor.com/research/labor-index/benchmark-map/ |
| 4 | I Love Software Rendering | 283 | https://www.jamesfmackenzie.com/2026/10/13/i-love-software-rendering/ |
| 5 | Waymo in Toronto | 264 | https://waymo.com/blog/2026/10/waymo-in-toronto/ |

Here is the same data as JSON:
```json
[
 {"title":"Tesla Roadster","points":1171,"url":"https://www.tesla.com/roadster"},
 {"title":"Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins","points":660,"url":"https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins"},
 {"title":"90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks","points":393,"url":"https://www.mercor.com/research/labor-index/benchmark-map/"},
 {"title":"I Love Software Rendering","points":283,"url":"https://www.jamesfmackenzie.com/2026/10/13/i-love-software-rendering/"},
 {"title":"Waymo in Toronto","points":264,"url":"https://waymo.com/blog/2026/10/waymo-in-toronto/"}
]
```

The endpoint was `https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?tags=front_page&hitsPerPage=5`. The front-page ordering in that API can lag slightly behind the live homepage, and points change as people vote.
